data.narrative:
Wisk Aero, a Series C frontier-aerospace company founded by Gary Gysin, has raised $450M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 13 peer companies in Space & Aerospace—5 publicly traded (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms at Series B through Series D stages, including Sierra Space, Impulse Space, and Varda Space Industries.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $450M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage transitions, yielding $765M. Peer-median analysis anchors to 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $2.0B (range: $1.15B–$8.0B). The public-comp method cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure. These two methods produce a triangulated range of $650M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.4B.

Key uncertainties include significant dispersion in the peer set—Sierra Space trades at $8.0B while lower-stage peers cluster below $2.5B—reflecting valuation sensitivity to technology maturity and capital efficiency. The wide gap between stage-progression and peer-median estimates reflects tension between recent fundraising history and sector comparables. Additional clarity on revenue trajectory, customer contracts, and technology readiness would materially refine this range.
